title: Vilasa 7. The Installation of the Six Deities and the Great Festival in Kheturi
html:
Talk of the festival; the preparations; on Phalguna-purnima Srinivasa performs the abhisheka of the six Deities; Narottama begins the sankirtana; the Lord with His associates appears in the kirtana; the Holi festival; the feeding of the Vaishnavas

1Glory to Gaura, Nityananda and Advaita with their associates!
Be merciful, Prabhu, to this wretched beggar.

2Glory, glory to the listeners, oceans of mercy!
Hear what I shall now relate.

3The news of the great festival in the village of Sri Kheturi
spread through every land.

4With great joy at heart people said to one another:
"O brother, what a marvel I have seen with my eyes!

5Blessed on all the earth is the village of Sri Kheturi —
what wondrous beauty, like an abode of bliss!

6Women and men, children and old people there
shed tears ceaselessly at the sight of the Vaishnavas.

7Today many Vaishnavas have come to Kheturi,
and people, forgetting themselves, run from all sides."

8Some, seeing that sweetness,
begged the Creator for countless eyes.

9Some said: "Their radiance is like the sun's;
it destroys the cruel darkness of the sufferings of living beings."

10Some said: "By the mercy of a glance from them
even one who would not say 'Krishna' sings Krishna's virtues."

11Some said: "Wondrous are their ways:
they have the greatest love for the fallen and suffering."

12Some said: "Fortunate is Raja Sri Santosha:
what wonderful lodgings he has made for them!"

13Some said: "In preparing the great festival
the raja and his people are always rejoicing."

14Some said: "The stores he has prepared —
I have no power to describe them."

15Some said: "All the auspicious rites customary among people
the raja performs with care."

16Some said: "On the bright fifth day of Phalguna
he told the musicians to begin playing."

17Some said: "The sound of the music pierced the sky;
singers sing, dancers dance."

18Some said: "The raja told the gardeners
to bring various flowers and carefully make garlands."

19Some said: "The raja told many people
to grind fine sandal carefully."

20Some said: "At the Mahashaya's command
they joyfully made ready the things for the abhisheka.

21Tomorrow is the holy full moon, a wondrous day:
the Deities will be ceremonially brought into the holy temple."

22Some said: "O brother, I cannot say it —
I shall leave everything and go quickly to Kheturi."

23Someone, after a silence, said: "This is what has happened:
Sri Thakura Mahashaya has made this land blessed.

24The people of this land are skilled in banditry;
they do not know what dharma is or what proper deeds are.

25Who could tell all the evil they do?
The blood of goats, sheep and buffaloes is at their doors."

26Some said: "Taking a severed human head,
sword in hand, they dance, intoxicated.

27If at that time anyone goes along that road,
even a brahmana does not escape their hands.

28All are lechers, with no regard for caste;
they never eat without wine and meat.

29O brother, I am firmly convinced:
Narottama will deliver them all."

30Crying "Glory to Narottama! Glory to Narottama!"
they danced with arms upraised, tears streaming from their eyes.

31Taking various gifts, in great excitement,
all came quickly to the village of Sri Kheturi.

32So from many villages came many people;
as soon as they entered Kheturi they forgot all grief.

33Meanwhile Sri Thakura Mahashaya, with sweet words,
dispelled the sorrows of all the people.

34Having arranged everything thus, with gladness of heart,
in the evening he said to the Acharya:

35"Many khols and karatalas have been made and brought here —
please go and look at them once."

36Hearing this, Sri Acharya went gladly,
taking Gauranga, Gokula and Devidasa with him.

37Going there and seeing all the khols and karatalas,
the Acharya said in prema, "Good, good!"

38Remembering Gaura, Nityananda and Advaita,
he at once performed puja of the khols and karatalas.

39With everyone he went to where Sri Ishvari was
and set out in order everything about the abhisheka.

40Receiving her permission, they went everywhere
and told everyone about the abhisheka.

41Hearing it, joy grew in everyone's heart,
and they spent that night in talks about Sri Chaitanya.

42They slept a little, and the night turned to morning;
all performed their morning duties and bathed.

43Meanwhile Sri Acharya and Sri Thakura Mahashaya
went to every lodging with wonderful cloths.

44To all the mahantas and all who were with the mahantas
they offered cloths with great insistence.

45Meanwhile Sri Santosha Raya, with great joy,
was seeing how well the canopy looked over the courtyard.

46The courtyard of the holy temple is very spacious
and adorned beautifully in every way.

47Beneath the canopy were wonderful seats,
on which the holy mahantas came and sat.

48The place where Sri Jahnava Ishvari sat
was well screened, near the assembly.

49Everywhere plantain trees beyond counting,
mango boughs hung with coconuts and other fruits,

50pitchers full of water shining everywhere.
Having seen all this, he went to where the Acharya was

51and reported that everything there was finely arranged.
Hearing it, the Acharya went to where Sri Ishvari was.

52When he informed her, she went
and sat in the screened place.

53When Sri Acharya informed all the mahantas,
all went and sat on the seats in the courtyard.

54A wondrous beauty appeared, surpassing a host of moons;
they showered one another with the nectar of words.

55All gave Acharya Thakura permission
to perform the abhisheka and other rites of the holy Deities.

56Sri Acharya, receiving the permission of the Ishvari and others,
bowed most humbly and went.

57He had the holy Deities brought into the holy temple,
and seeing their beauty the Acharya was overwhelmed.

58Clasping to his heart the Moon of Navadvipa with Lakshmi and Vishnupriya,
he wept, remembering His virtues.

59Who can understand the Acharya's heart?
After a while the wisest one grew calm.

60According to the rules of the books composed by Sri Rupa Gosvami
he performed all the rites with the greatest care.1

61The names Prabhu had made known in the dream
all clearly resounded at the abhisheka:

62Gauranga, Vallavikanta, Sri Vrajamohana,
Sri Krishna, Sri Radhakanta, Sri Radharamana.

63So the holy Deities took their seats on the thrones —
a wondrous beauty together with their Beloveds, dear as life.

64Seeing Their bodies adorned with various ornaments,
the Acharya was filled with great bliss.

65Finishing the puja, he quickly performed arati
and offered food to each separately.

66All those foods were most wonderful:
things to chew, suck, lick and drink, of many kinds.

67The Lords ate in supreme bliss;
after a while the offering was carefully removed.

68Quickly washing the place of the meal,
he offered plates filled with holy garlands and sandal.

69He placed garlands with sandal on the Lords' necks
and, dividing the rest, kept some apart.

70On separate plates the holy garlands and sandal
he offered before all the mahantas.

71All, rejoicing together in prema,
adorned themselves with the holy garlands and sandal.

72Seeing the six holy Deities together,
everyone cried out "Jaya! Jaya!"

73Many instruments played, a tumult arose —
as though all that is inauspicious had left the world.

74Then everyone gave Sri Thakura Mahashaya
permission to begin the sankirtana.

75Sri Thakura Mahashaya, with gladness of heart,
told Devidasa to make ready.

76Devidasa, with the singers and musicians,
came joyfully into Gauranga's courtyard.

77Vallabha, Gauranga, Gokula and other dear ones —
their beauty stole everyone's heart.

78Taking them with him, Sri Thakura Mahashaya,
all radiant, stood in the courtyard.

79His body, wrapped in thrills, beautifully formed,
its lustre surpassing golden ketaki.

80A prominent nose, long lotus eyes —
seeing that face, Kandarpa's pride goes far away.

81A pair of lovely arms surpassing an elephant's trunk;
who would not rejoice to see the beauty of his chest?

82How the tilaka gleams on his lovely forehead!
His neck shines with tulasi beads.

83How sweet are his lovely feet, knees and waist!
To look on them takes away the burning of the eyes.

84The supreme, wondrous beauty cannot be told;
what jubilation in his heart at the start of the sankirtana!

85Remembering Nitai, Advaita and Gorachand with their associates,
he overflowed with prema and could not contain himself.

86Bowing to the ground before all the mahantas,
he took the karatalas in his hands and began the alapa.2

87In a gentle smile his teeth shone beautifully;
he was covered with sweat and tears, with great bliss at heart.

88Thus in the Stavamrita-lahari:
To him whose face lit up the quarters with the radiance of his teeth
in the gentle smile born of the bliss of sankirtana,
who was bathed in streams of sweat and tears —
to Sri Narottama, obeisances, obeisances!

89On Devidasa and others he had earlier bestowed power;
now, at his direction, they became intoxicated in song and music.

90The mridangas sounded, sweet as nectar;
the alapa, the karatalas and the music blended together.

91Sri Raghunandana could not contain himself:
like a maddened lion he roared, remembering Gauranga.

92The Acharya brought holy garlands and sandal
and at once touched them to the khols and karatalas.

93Sri Raghunandana, forgetting himself in prema,
smeared Narottama with sandal with his own hands,

94put a garland on him and embraced him firmly;
in the same way he gave holy garlands and sandal to all.

95All, bowing at Raghunandana's feet,
with all their hearts deemed themselves blessed.

96Sri Gauranga Dasa began to beat the tala;3
at first the instruments sounded very softly,

97and then new and new things swelled moment by moment,
as shoots of nectar grow thick and fast.

98Hearing the wondrous, wondrous music, the gods
with the gandharvas and kinnaras filled the sky,

99and, wholly losing composure, they showered flowers
and, mingling with men, fulfilled their longing.

100Meanwhile all the mahantas said to one another:
"This is Prabhu's wondrous creation through Narottama.

101Such music full of prema we have never heard,
such a mode of singing we have never seen.

102Narottama's voice is a stream of nectar:
whoever drinks it feels his thirst grow ceaselessly.

103What wondrous turns he shows in his singing!
Do the gandharvas and kinnaras know their secret?

104The Moon of Navadvipa, Prabhu, the son of Sri Shachi —
surely it was for this that He drew him long ago.

105Subdued by Narottama's prema, Prabhu
has entrusted to Narottama the treasury of song and music."

106Saying this, they embraced Narottama
and all began to dance like madmen.

107What wondrous tears of bliss in everyone's eyes!
Their bodies shone with holy garlands and sandal.

108Narottama, intoxicated, sang Hari's virtues,
and Gaura Raya with His associates lost His composure.

109Nityananda, Advaita, Srivasa, Gadadhara,
Murari, Svarupa, Haridasa, Vakreshvara,

110Jagadisha, Gauridasa and all the others
joyfully became visible to everyone's eyes.4

111At that moment all forgot themselves —
as if they were sporting joyfully in Navadvipa.

112Sri Achyutananda and others danced,
and with them danced the son of Shachi.

113Prabhu Nityananda, with great gladness of heart,
danced beside his dear Narottama.

114Prabhu Sri Advaita danced in great intoxication,
taking with him Ramachandra, Shyamananda and all the others.

115Pandita Gadadhara danced in the joy of prema,
bringing Srinivasa Acharya to Prabhu.

116In the same great festivity danced Pandita Srivasa,
Sri Murari Gupta, Sri Svarupa, Haridasa,

117Shriman Pandita, the brahmachari Shuklambara,
Vasudeva Datta, Sri Pandita Vakreshvara,

118Gadadhara Dasa, Sri Mukunda, Narahari,
Gauridasa Pandita, Nakula Brahmachari,

119Jagadisha, Suryadasa, Acharya-nandana,
Shrinatha, Mahesha, Yadu, Sri Madhusudana,

120Govinda, Madhava, Vasu, Ramananda Raya,
Sri Vijaya, Dhananjaya, Datta Sri Mukunda,

121Sanatana, Rupa, Raghunatha, Kashishvara —
countless associates of Sri Prabhu danced.

122The turns of their dance intoxicate the world with delight;
at the movement of their feet the earth trembles.

123The manifest and the unmanifest came together in one place —
what a wondrous dance! No one remembers the body.

124At the supremely intoxicating music the heart exults;
all roar, clapping their hands.

125Who can hold himself up, drinking the nectar of the song?
Moment by moment waves of various bhavas arise.

126The Moon of Navadvipa, casting His glance in all directions,
showers the nectar of prema, rare even for the gods.

127Countless people were maddened and could not restrain themselves;
everywhere they wept, crying "Sri Krishna Chaitanya!"

128What Prabhu had told Narottama in the dream
He revealed to all, rejoicing.5

129Who can understand this unearthly pastime of Prabhu?
As He appeared, so He vanished.

130When Prabhu vanished, all were stunned:
in that ecstasy all lost consciousness.

131Though all these wise ones had forgotten everything,
they lamented, overwhelmed by separation:

132"Alas, alas, what a marvel we have just seen!
Where have Gaura and Nityananda, jewels of virtue, gone?

133Where have Advaita, Srivasa, Gadadhara gone?
Where are Sri Murari, Haridasa, Vakreshvara?

134Where are Narahari, Gauridasa and the Lord's other associates?" —
so, taking their names, all wept.

135Sri Jahnava Ishvari could not contain herself:
"Having shown Himself, where has He gone?" she said and wept.

136Sri Achyutananda and all the dear ones
said weeping: "What dream have we seen?"

137Srinivasa and Narottama, when Prabhu disappeared,
at once threw themselves to the ground.

138"Alas, alas, what has happened!" they cried and wept;
hearing that weeping, wood and stone melt.

139Ramachandra, Shyamananda and others all around —
who could keep composure at their weeping?

140Hundreds of thousands of people wept, and the tears from their eyes
flowed in streams over the ground like the current of a river.

141The pashandis who had come to mock —
all their hearts were turned; they wept in distress.

142No one could leave Gauranga's courtyard;
the state they were all in cannot be described.

143The brahmana Vaninatha and others, who had lain unconscious,
after a while came to their senses and grew calm.

144So all grew calm by Prabhu's will
and saw Srinivasa Acharya rolling on the ground,

145and Narottama, Ramachandra, Sri Gokulananda,
Shridasa, Sri Shyamananda, Gokula, Govinda,

146Sri Rasikananda, Devidasa and all the others
lying unconscious on the ground.

147By the efforts of all the mahantas they
came to consciousness, but could not compose themselves.

148After a while, growing calm and checking their weeping,
Sri Acharya and Narottama lamented much.

149Sri Jahnava Ishvari, in a sweet, gentle voice,
said privately to Narottama and Srinivasa:

150"Hearing this grief, the heart breaks;
check your grief, remembering Prabhu's command.

151Now is just the time to begin the play with colored powder."6
Hearing and remembering, they rejoiced at heart.

152Bowing at the feet of Sri Jahnava Ishvari,
they went with everyone to the mahantas.

153Acharya Thakura and the Mahashaya with their people
consoled Sri Achyutananda and all the others:

154"Nityananda, Advaita and Gaura with Their associates
are in every way subdued by your prema.

155Birth after birth you are servants of Prabhu;
He is always visible to your eyes."

156They said: "May the bliss we found in your kirtana
remain in our hearts birth after birth."

157Saying this, they embraced everyone,
bathed in tears, unable to contain themselves.

158Srinivasa, Narottama and all the others
bowed in prema at the feet of all.

159The bliss they all shared at that moment —
is it possible to tell it with one mouth?

160Srinivasa Acharya and Thakura Mahashaya
respectfully addressed all the mahantas:

161"Offering colored powder to Prabhu's holy body,
begin the play with powder together with everyone."

162As soon as they heard it, everyone's heart rejoiced;
at that moment Sri Santosha came bringing powder —

163of various kinds, fragrant and lovely,
in separate dishes, delightfully beautiful.

164So much powder was brought that it could not be counted;
everything around became powder, a marvel to see.

165Sri Thakura Mahashaya with Ramachandra
arranged powder beautifully before Sri Ishvari.

166Taking the powder, the Ishvari went into the holy temple,
put powder on Prabhu's body and gazed her fill.

167Losing her composure, she came back into seclusion
and could not check the tears from both her eyes.

168Meanwhile Sri Achyuta, Raghunandana, Shrinidhi,
Vaninatha, Hridaya Chaitanya, Yadu and others —

169all the mahantas, joyfully taking powder,
put it on Gauranga's body and laughed in prema.

170Some, putting it on Radhakanta and Sri Vallavikanta,
spoke with great joy of the pastimes of Vraja.

171Some playfully put powder on Krishna with Radha,
some put powder on Vrajamohana's body.

172Someone, putting powder on Radharamana's body,
lost composure, gazing at that lovely beauty.

173Having thus offered powder to the Lords,
they began, overwhelmed, to throw powder at one another.

174Some recited verses of the Holi-yatra at will,
some sang of the pastimes of Navadvipa and Vrindavana,

175some went about beating drums, some danced,
some, powder in hand, ran after someone.

176Hundreds of thousands of people all around played with powder;
the powder flew upward and covered the sky.

177Gods and men came together in one gathering;
there is nothing in the world to compare with such a powder-play.

178Srinivasa Acharya and others, with gladness of heart,
adorned with powder, went about everywhere.

179The wondrous powder-play went on for a long time —
who has the power to describe it?

180When all the mahantas grew calm, evening had come;
seeing Prabhu's arati they soothed their eyes.

181For a while, intoxicated with the holy name,
all sat again in Prabhu's courtyard.

182The rites of Prabhu's birth-day — abhisheka and so on —
the Acharya performed with all care.7

183All the mahantas, with great bliss at heart,
sang songs of Gauranga's birth in soft voices.

184Cymbals and mridangas sounded, sweet as nectar;
some danced a dance that enchants the world.

185The song, dance and music have no comparison;
the bliss there was — who could describe it?

186So in prema all passed the night,
and when the night turned to morning they performed their morning duties.

187Meanwhile Sri Jahnava Devi, at the very dawn,
having finished her morning duties, bathed in warm water.

188Having performed her daily rites, with gladness of heart
she went to the kitchen, taking Srinivasa with her.

189Seeing all the provisions for cooking ready,
she said to the Acharya with a slight smile:

190"I brought you here
to tell you to fetch various things —

191and you have made everything ready here so quickly!
How did you know that I would cook like this?"

192Saying this, the Ishvari sat on a low stool
and cooked with every care.

193Seeing the fine skill of the servants,
she praised them all with great joy.

194The Ishvari's cooking is an unearthly play:
one cannot follow how she accomplishes it.

195Quickly cooking rice and various dishes,
she carefully arranged the rice on wonderful platters.

196Filling many vessels with various dishes,
the Ishvari hastened to offer the food.

197Admiring the beauty of each separate offering,
she offered the food to the Lords with great joy —

198to Gauranga, Vallavikanta, Sri Radhamohana,
Radhakanta, Radha-Krishna, Sri Vrajamohana.8

199All ate joyfully with various playful ways,
praising all the wonderful, most delicious dishes.

200Sri Jahnava Ishvari, seeing that play,
was overwhelmed with prema and could not be calm.

201As is the custom among people, quickly drawing the curtain,
the Ishvari came out of the temple.

202When the play of the meal here was over,
she went, as is the custom, to remove the offering,

203gave water for rinsing and offered betel;
the play there was cannot be described.

204Meanwhile all the mahantas finished their bathing and rites,
and the Acharya came bringing prasada:

205sweets, fried delicacies and so on, sweet as nectar —
all ate them in supreme bliss.

206Acharya Thakura announced everywhere
that the time for the raja-bhoga arati had come.

207Hearing it, all went to Prabhu's courtyard,
and at the sight of the arati there was supreme bliss.

208The pujari, performing arati with joy at heart,
gave everyone prasada garlands and tulasi.

209Garlands of wonderful flowers on everyone's neck —
seeing this, all the people soothed their eyes.

210Meanwhile, preparing lovely beds in various places,
the pujari laid the Lords to rest,

211carefully covering Them with wonderful cloths,
pressing Their feet and waving a lovely chamara.

212Having served thus, he quickly came outside,
closed the doors and bowed to the ground,

213offered many prayers and went away;
how fine the service was I cannot describe.

214Meanwhile Srinivasa Acharya said to everyone:
"We shall eat here, in Prabhu's courtyard."

215Srinivasa swept the dust from the courtyard,
and all the mahantas sat in a circle.

216All asked for plantain leaves to be brought,
and wonderful leaves were brought as everyone wished.

217Some carefully laid out the leaves,
some filled vessels with scented water,

218some brought vessels of ghee, curd and milk,
some put salt on pieces of leaf.

219What Sri Jahnava Ishvari felt on seeing that circle —
who could say?

220Quickly rice and dishes were served row on row;
the fragrance of rice and dishes stole the heart.

221Of greens and fried dishes there was no counting,
soups, sour dishes and sweet rice of many kinds.

222All ate with gladness of heart;
seeing that beauty, life and eyes were soothed.

223Having eaten joyfully and rinsed their mouths,
they said to one another, "We have eaten a great deal."

224Sri Achyutananda and others said softly:
"How we ate so much we cannot understand."

225Shripati, Shrinidhi, Vaninatha and others said:
"Surely we ate so much by the Ishvari's power."

226Sri Raghunandana and others said again and again:
"We shall never again eat with such happiness."

227As soon as they said this, all were bathed in tears,
and with great effort all regained composure.

228Acharya Thakura and Sri Thakura Mahashaya,
going to the Ishvari, said respectfully:

229"You have toiled greatly; now, sitting in seclusion,
please partake of prasada — this is our wish."

230The Ishvari said: "I have a great longing:
to feed all of you, and to eat afterwards myself.

231Take everyone and sit quickly in the courtyard;
if you say anything against it, you are bound by an oath to me."

232Hearing this, the Acharya quickly took everyone,
and they sat in a circle in Prabhu's courtyard.

233Seeing the leaves and the rest laid out as before,
the Ishvari, with joy at heart, served in order.

234With the greatest affection she fed everyone,
and all ate happily, remembering Prabhu's deeds.

235Tasting the supreme flavour, with gladness of heart,
they said to one another in sweet words:

236"This cooking of holy hands is rare even for the gods:
never since we were born have we eaten such greens!"

237So, praising the various dishes, they ate
and with great joy deemed themselves blessed.

238Meanwhile Raghunandana and others, overwhelmed by affection,
having watched the beauty of the meal, went to their lodgings.

239Having finished the meal, there rose Srinivasa,
Narottama, Ramachandra, Govinda, Shridasa,

240Ramakrishna, Kumuda, Gokulananda, Vyasa,
Shyamananda, Sri Krishnavallabha, Devidasa,

241Bhagavan, Nrisimha, Gokula, Karnapura,
Kishora, Rasikananda, Gauranga Thakura,

242Sri Gopiramana and others; having rinsed their mouths,
all chewed prasada betel.

243Sri Acharya went quickly to Sri Ishvari
and carefully prepared a place for her meal in seclusion.

244Sri Jahnava Ishvari, with supreme joy at heart,
taking all the dishes, sat down to eat.

245Sri Acharya Thakura with Sri Shyamananda
fed many people, serving them with care.

246The pujari Sri Balarama and some others
ate last of all.

247Sri Jahnava Ishvari, having finished her meal,
came into seclusion and bathed in warm water.

248The Ishvari's attendant, a brahmana's wife,
carefully dried her body with a fine cloth.

249Burned incessantly by the fire of separation from Prabhu,
her body, like a golden lotus, had become very thin.

250Drying her body with the greatest care,
she had another bring her clothing.

251Putting on a dry, clean cloth, the Ishvari sat on her seat,
ate a piece of haritaki and rinsed her mouth.

252To Narottama she said affectionately:
"After so many days, today I have eaten my fill."

253Narottama, remembering Nityananda and Chaitanya,
shed streams from both eyes and kept silent.

254Sri Jahnava Ishvari, in prema,
calmed Narottama with sweet words.

255Srinivasa Acharya together with Sri Shyamananda
came joyfully to Sri Ishvari.

256Sri Jahnava Ishvari, with supreme joy at heart,
said to the Acharya in sweet words:

257"It is not good to delay going to Vrindavana;
I think to set out tomorrow morning."

258The Acharya said: "I can say nothing:
my heart breaks to hear these words.

259What you have willed cannot be otherwise:
you will surely go to Vrindavana.

260Everything needed for the journey has been arranged here."
Hearing this, she smiled slightly.

261The Acharya added humbly:
"It would be good for you to lie down a little."

262Hearing this, she lay down on that same seat,
and the three quickly went elsewhere.

263After resting a while, the three
went to Sri Achyutananda's house.

264All the mahantas were sitting there,
absorbed in talks about Krishna.

265At the coming of these three their happiness increased;
I cannot describe all those talks here.

266After a while all said to the Acharya:
"Asking leave to go — we do not know what our hearts are doing.

267You know everything — what more can we say?
All wish to leave tomorrow morning."

268The Acharya said: "What you have willed —
who has the power to make it otherwise?

269We think that tomorrow, very early,
it would be good to have food cooked in each lodging,

270to finish bathing and so on quickly
and eat with joy — the fortunate will see it."

271Hearing the Acharya's words, all were amused
and said, laughing, "As you wish."

272Saying this and staying a little longer,
all went to their own lodgings.

273Acharya Thakura and Sri Thakura Mahashaya
with Shyamananda came to Prabhu's temple.

274Sri Santosha Raya and others came there,
and the Acharya told them everything.

275Whoever rejoices to hear all these accounts
will surely have his desire fulfilled.

276Listen to all this continually and with care:
Narahari tells the Narottama-vilasa.9

Thus ends the seventh vilasa of the Narottama-vilasa.

Notes

  1. That is, according to the manuals of Deity worship associated with the name of Rupa Gosvami.
  2. Alapa: the introductory singing of the melody without words before the kirtana.
  3. Tala-pata: the rhythmic opening (the beat) of the kirtana.
  4. That is, the Lord with His long-departed associates became visible in Narottama's kirtana, as he had been promised in the dream (Vilasa 4).
  5. See Vilasa 4, vv. 150–154.
  6. Phalguna-purnima is the Dola (Holi) festival, when the Deities and one another are sprinkled with colored powder (phagu).
